memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The LORD also said to Moses, 'This is the offering Aaron and his sons are to bring to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of the finest flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half in the evening.'" - Lev 6:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The priest who receives everyone else's offerings must also bring his own.

That is easy to overlook and important to notice. Aaron spent his days handling other people's worship. God made sure he had worship of his own to bring.

There is a real danger for anyone who serves. The pastor who prepares sermons can stop reading Scripture for himself. The worship leader can stop worshipping. The person who prays for everyone can stop praying for their own soul. Handling holy things becomes a profession rather than a relationship.

Notice also the rhythm: half in the morning, half in the evening. Twice daily, every day. Not dramatic, just steady.

Paul warned Timothy, Watch your life and doctrine closely (1 Tim 4:16) — life first. And he told the Ephesian elders, Keep watch over yourselves and all the flock (Acts 20:28) — yourselves before the flock.

If you serve God in any capacity, ask yourself an honest question: when did you last come to God with nothing to prepare, nothing to lead, nothing to produce — just yourself?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has my service to God begun to replace my relationship with God?
2. When did I last come to God purely as a worshipper rather than a worker?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from handling holy things while my own heart grows cold. I come to You today not to serve but simply to be with You. Amen.
